references.text: The priest receives a portion of the offering as his property, confirming the principle that what is given to the priest belongs to him.
Moses instructs Aaron and his sons about their right to the holy offerings, affirming the priests' ownership of the sacrificial gifts.
The Lord gives Aaron and his descendants the holy offerings as a perpetual right, elaborating on the principle of the priests' entitlement to the offerings.
All holy gifts that the Israelites bring to the Lord are given to Aaron and his descendants as an everlasting covenant.
Describes the priests' rightful share of the people's sacrifices, including the firstfruits.
Ezekiel describes the priests' right to grain offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings, as well as the firstfruits of everything.
Paul refers to the principle that those who serve in the temple get their food from the temple, applying it to preachers of the gospel.
